results.name: mult4_set_even_nonmult4_yes
results.description: Among sets (>=2 examples) whose examples are all multiples of 4, the "yes" rate for even targets not divisible by 4 (and not in the set); observed below null = model over-predicts acceptance of merely-even numbers (even/even-in-range concepts) when a multiples-of-4/8 rule fits.
results.code:
# name: mult4_set_even_nonmult4_yes
# description: Among sets (>=2 examples) whose examples are all multiples of 4, the "yes" rate for even targets not divisible by 4 (and not in the set); observed below null = model over-predicts acceptance of merely-even numbers (even/even-in-range concepts) when a multiples-of-4/8 rule fits.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    all4 = ((ex % 4 == 0) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    m = all4 & (t % 2 == 0) & (t % 4 != 0) & ~inset
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[m, "rating"].mean())

results.name: round_target_yes_in_nonround_sets
results.description: "Yes" rate for round targets (multiples of 10, including 100) in sets containing no multiple of 10; observed above null = a round-number acceptance bias the model under-produces, below = model over-produces "yes" to round numbers (e.g. via ranges ending at 100).

results.name: two_example_interior_yes
results.description: For two-example sets, the "yes" rate for targets strictly between the two examples that share neither example's last digit; observed below null = model's range concepts over-produce interior "yes" for two-example sets (people stay rule-bound), above = people interpolate more than the model.
results.code:
# name: two_example_interior_yes
# description: For two-example sets, the "yes" rate for targets strictly between the two examples that share neither example's last digit; observed below null = model's range concepts over-produce interior "yes" for two-example sets (people stay rule-bound), above = people interpolate more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    lo, hi = ex.min(axis=1), ex.max(axis=1)
    sharedig = ex.mod(10).eq(t % 10, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    m = (n == 2) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~sharedig
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[m, "rating"].mean())

results.name: near_example_yes_rate
results.description: In sets with >=3 examples, the "yes" rate for targets 1-2 away from the nearest example (not in the set) minus the rate for targets 3-10 away; observed above null = people show a sharper local-similarity gradient than the model's range/rule mixture produces.
results.code:
# name: near_example_yes_rate
# description: In sets with >=3 examples, the "yes" rate for targets 1-2 away from the nearest example (not in the set) minus the rate for targets 3-10 away; observed above null = people show a sharper local-similarity gradient than the model's range/rule mixture produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    dist = ex.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    near = (n >= 3) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 2)
    mid = (n >= 3) & (dist >= 3) & (dist <= 10)
    if near.sum() == 0 or mid.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[near, "rating"].mean() - df.loc[mid, "rating"].mean())

results.name: shared_last_digit_offdigit_inrange_yes
results.description: Among sets (>=2 examples) whose examples all end in the same digit, the "yes" rate for targets inside [min,max] of the examples that do NOT end in that digit; observed below null = model over-generalises via (parity-)range concepts when a last-digit rule is evident.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_offdigit_inrange_yes
# description: Among sets (>=2 examples) whose examples all end in the same digit, the "yes" rate for targets inside [min,max] of the examples that do NOT end in that digit; observed below null = model over-generalises via (parity-)range concepts when a last-digit rule is evident.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    last = ex % 10
    same = (last.nunique(axis=1) == 1) & (n >= 2)
    d = last.iloc[:, 0]
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    lo, hi = ex.min(axis=1), ex.max(axis=1)
    m = same & (t % 10 != d) & (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[m, "rating"].mean())

results.name: inrange_cell_yes_variance
results.description: Variance across (set,target) cells of the cell "yes" rate, among cells whose target lies inside the examples' range in sets with >=3 examples; observed above null = people's in-range judgements are more all-or-none (more polarised by target) than the model's graded predictions.
results.code:
# name: inrange_cell_yes_variance
# description: Variance across (set,target) cells of the cell "yes" rate, among cells whose target lies inside the examples' range in sets with >=3 examples; observed above null = people's in-range judgements are more all-or-none (more polarised by target) than the model's graded predictions.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    lo, hi = ex.min(axis=1), ex.max(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 3) & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    sub = df.loc[m]
    if len(sub) == 0:
        return 0.0
    cm = sub.groupby(["number_set", "target"])["rating"].mean()
    return float(cm.var(ddof=0))

results.name: odd_mult3_set_odd_minus_even_multiple
results.description: In sets whose examples are all odd multiples of 3, the "yes" rate for odd multiple-of-3 targets minus that for even multiple-of-3 targets; observed above null = people use a conjunctive "odd multiples of 3" concept the model lacks (model under-produces the contrast), below = model over-weights parity.
results.code:
# name: odd_mult3_set_odd_minus_even_multiple
# description: In sets whose examples are all odd multiples of 3, the "yes" rate for odd multiple-of-3 targets minus that for even multiple-of-3 targets; observed above null = people use a conjunctive "odd multiples of 3" concept the model lacks (model under-produces the contrast), below = model over-weights parity.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    ok = (((ex % 3 == 0) & (ex % 2 == 1)) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    m3 = ok & (t % 3 == 0)
    odd = m3 & (t % 2 == 1)
    even = m3 & (t % 2 == 0)
    if odd.sum() == 0 or even.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[odd, "rating"].mean() - df.loc[even, "rating"].mean())

results.name: odd_set_far_beyond_range_yes
results.description: In sets (>=3 examples) of all-odd numbers, the "yes" rate for odd targets more than 15 beyond the examples' range minus that for odd targets inside the range; observed above null (less negative) = people extend "odd" beyond the range more than the model's odd-within-range concepts allow.
results.code:
# name: odd_set_far_beyond_range_yes
# description: In sets (>=3 examples) of all-odd numbers, the "yes" rate for odd targets more than 15 beyond the examples' range minus that for odd targets inside the range; observed above null (less negative) = people extend "odd" beyond the range more than the model's odd-within-range concepts allow.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    allodd = ((ex % 2 == 1) | ex.isna()).all(axis=1) & (n >= 3)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    lo, hi = ex.min(axis=1), ex.max(axis=1)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    oddt = allodd & (t % 2 == 1) & ~inset
    far = oddt & ((t > hi + 15) | (t < lo - 15))
    inside = oddt & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    if far.sum() == 0 or inside.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[far, "rating"].mean() - df.loc[inside, "rating"].mean())
